About the Role

We're looking for a Growth and Demand Marketing Manager to build and run our demand generation engine from the ground up. This is a hands-on, generalist role on a small team — you'll set lifecycle marketing strategy, execute campaigns, create content, and personally generate qualified opportunities for sales. You'll work closely with our Brand Marketing Manager, Event Marketing Manager, and Director of Product Marketing, but you should be comfortable owning your own work end-to-end rather than directing others to do it. As we scale, this role has a clear path to leading a broader growth and demand generation function.
 
You Will...
 
Develop and execute lifecycle marketing programs — including nurture tracks and email campaigns — that guide senior technology decision makers in logistics through awareness, consideration, and conversion.
Drive marketing qualified leads (MQLs) that convert into sales opportunities and ultimately customer acquisition.
Spend roughly 20% of your time proactively prospecting and qualifying senior logistics-technology decision makers yourself — giving you direct control over your own funnel's quality, not just its volume — and handing sales-ready opportunities to the sales team.
Track customer acquisition cost by channel and campaign; use that data to continuously refine messaging, targeting, and channel mix.
Own lower-funnel digital campaigns — paid search/social, retargeting — and account-based marketing programs targeting senior logistics decision makers at named accounts. Brand and upper-funnel awareness campaigns are owned by the
Brand Marketing Manager.
Partner with the Brand Marketing Manager, Event Marketing Manager, and Director of Product Marketing to plan and deploy integrated campaigns — including email and nurture programs — that increase commercial velocity.
Build and manage segmented email nurture campaigns that move leads through the funnel, keeping messaging relevant to where each prospect is in their buying journey.
Write white papers, host webinars, and produce other thought leadership content — using AI tools to accelerate production where useful — that resonates with senior logistics technology buyers and drives measurable lead flow.
 
What Success Looks Like
 
In your first 6–12 months, you will have:
Lifecycle engine: Built and are running a repeatable lifecycle marketing engine — including active nurture and email programs — generating a predictable, growing volume of MQLs and opportunities each month.
Pipeline contribution: Personally sourced and qualified a meaningful share of sales opportunities through your own outbound prospecting.
CAC discipline: Established CAC tracking by channel and used it to shift spend toward what converts best with logistics technology buyers.
Digital & ABM impact: Built and optimized lower-funnel and ABM campaigns with measurable pipeline contribution from target accounts.
Content impact: Published thought-leadership content (white papers, webinars) with clear, attributable pipeline impact.
 
Qualifications
 
Required
6+ years in B2B marketing, demand generation, or growth marketing, ideally at a small or early-stage company.
Track record building and optimizing lead-gen and lifecycle programs — including email nurture campaigns — from strategy through execution.
Comfort and success doing hands-on outbound/prospecting work alongside strategic marketing work.
Experience measuring and optimizing against CAC or similar funnel metrics.
Strong analytical skills — comfortable pulling and interpreting campaign, funnel, and CAC data to drive decisions (Excel/Sheets required; SQL or BI tool experience a plus).
Strong writer — able to independently produce thought leadership content (white papers, webinars) and email copy.
Hands-on experience deploying AI tools in a marketing workflow, not just familiarity with them.
omfortable operating without a large team — self-directed, resourceful, willing to do unglamorous work.
Open-minded and collaborative team player with the willingness to help others.
Passionate about self-driving technologies, solving hard problems, and creating innovative solutions.
 
Bonus/nice to have
Experience marketing to senior technology decision makers in logistics, supply chain, or adjacent industrial/B2B sectors
Experience running account-based marketing (ABM) programs targeting named accounts
Experience partnering cross-functionally with product marketing, digital marketing, and events peers
Familiarity with a modern marketing/sales stack, particularly HubSpot and Aurasell (our CRM)
Experience at a company of similar size/stage
Prior SDR or sales development experience

The Role

The Cluster engineering team owns the software that turns thousands of wafers, servers, and switches into a cloud that stays up, stays busy, and stays debuggable. We stand clusters up from bare metal, schedule training and inference workloads across the fleet, keep it healthy, and make it observable to users, operators, and increasingly to AI agents. The stack is Go and Python on Kubernetes, running both on-premise deployments and our own cloud.

Responsibilities

· Declarative, CRD-driven automation of bare-metal networking, OS, and application software across clusters of Cerebras systems, servers, and switches, built to reconcile thousands of nodes

· Push-button cluster install, upgrade, and security patching with real downtime budgets, gated by canaries

· Kubernetes operators that schedule large inference workload: resource locks, priority queues, network topology, and health-aware placement

· gRPC control-plane services, authorization, admission webhooks, and quota policy for a multi-tenant fleet

· Metrics and log pipelines with purpose-built exporters for wafer-scale systems, servers (Redfish, IPMI), and network fabric (gNMI, sFlow), on Prometheus and Grafana, with SLOs and alerting

· Failure detection, HA control planes, and automated recovery, plus the CLIs, APIs, and MCP gateway that expose the fleet to users, operators, and AI agents

Skills and Qualifications

· 5+ years building and operating production distributed systems or infrastructure software

· Production-quality Go and Python

· Real Kubernetes depth: you have written or debugged controllers and operators, and you understand CRDs, reconciliation semantics, informer caches, admission webhooks, and RBAC

· Strong debugging skills across distributed systems, Linux, and networking

· Prometheus and Grafana as a practitioner: PromQL, exporter design, cardinality discipline, useful alerts

· Strong self-driving capability. This environment is large, fast-moving, and not fully documented, so we need engineers who build their own context, decide, and drive work across team boundaries. Learning speed matters more here than familiarity with our stack.

· Demonstrated adoption of AI in your engineering workflow: active use of coding agents, a view on where they help and where they mislead, and the rigor to verify what they produce.

· Nice to have: bare-metal or HPC fleet operations, scheduler internals, RDMA/RoCE and eBPF networking, Ceph or NVMe-oF, etcd and HA upgrades, inference serving stacks. ML research experience is not required.

Vous serez la personne qui définit le produit : comment les capacités sont regroupées et tarifées, comment les partenaires les découvrent et les intègrent, et comment la place de marché évolue en tant que plateforme d'affaires. The individual will be responsible for bringing structure to complex bodies of work, tracking progress, anticipating risks and dependencies, facilitating issue resolution, and ensuring stakeholders have clear visibility into activities and next steps.

In 1965, an engineer in Scotland was given a mundane task with a tricky problem to it - banks wanted to close on Saturdays and still serve customers, but they didn’t know how to solve the authentication of the right user. James Goodfellow, working at Smiths Industries, uncovered the insights that you needed something you have (a card) and something you know (a PIN). Because someone told him they could only remember 4 digits instead of his proposed 6, today over 3 million ATMs use a card+4 digit PIN over 60 years later. 
 Like the ATM, Mercury is building technology that pushes forward financial interfaces for the long term. Command is Mercury's LLM-powered financial assistant, launched to all customers in June 2026. It lets users understand their finances and take action in plain language, from asking about cash flow to sending payments, issuing cards, and managing invoices. With the product now in customers' hands, the work is to evolve it, extend its capabilities, and find new ways to leverage LLMs to give Mercury customers a more powerful banking* experience.
 What you'll do 
 Ship new capabilities users love:
 Design and ship new Command skills, the domain-specific instruction sets that teach the model how to handle workflows like sending money, managing invoices, and understanding cash flow
 Design and build agentic workflows in Command, defining the architecture for how multi-step agent interactions should work as we extend what the product can do on a customer's behalf
 Work with backend teams to define tool schemas for new capabilities, shaping the data contracts between Mercury's business logic and the model
 Own new capabilities end to end, from the system prompt to the frontend component that renders the response
 Own the LLM layer:
 Maintain and evolve Command's prompt architecture: the system prompt, skill loading system, session context, and the policy and compliance layers underneath
 Tune model behavior: reasoning effort, prompt caching strategy, fallback chains, and the streaming patterns that make the product feel fast
 Stay current with how models are evolving and bring that knowledge back to how Command is built
 Build quality in:
 Write and expand Command's eval harness, adding cases that cover new capabilities and scoring rubrics that detect regressions before users do
 Partner with product and compliance teams to define what "working correctly" means for each new capability, then build the tests that prove it
 Own the reliability and quality of what you ship, from initial design through post-launch monitoring
 This list is illustrative. Command is a product in motion and priorities will shift as we learn. The right person will help choose the next highest-leverage work.
 The ideal candidate 
 Has 7 or more years of software engineering experience, with deep technical expertise building and scaling LLM-powered applications in production
 Has gone beyond shipping a first version: you have scaled an LLM-powered product, dealt with the reliability and performance problems that come with real usage, and made it better over time
 Has experience designing agentic systems and has opinions about how to architect multi-step workflows that are reliable, explainable, and safe to run on behalf of real users
 Has built eval infrastructure and can write cases that actually measure whether the product works, not just whether the model outputs something plausible
 Understands the real tradeoffs in LLM deployments: latency, cost, compliance, and what breaks in production that doesn't show up in demos
 Has opinions about what makes an AI product trustworthy, not just impressive, and can build toward that bar
 Is comfortable with TypeScript and willing to learn Haskell for backend tool work, or already comfortable with both
 Can work across the full stack of an AI product, from the system prompt to the streaming frontend

 Chaussures Browns est à la recherche d’un(e) ingénieur(e) de données pragmatique et soucieux(se) des détails afin de concevoir et de maintenir des flux de données fiables entre nos applications d’affaires, nos partenaires externes et notre plateforme de données.

 Développer des intégrations basées sur des API, des transferts de fichiers et des bases de données à l’aide des outils d’intégration et des langages de programmation appropriés.
 Mettre en œuvre la logique d’extraction, d’ingestion, de validation et de cartographie source-cible, y compris les transformations requises pour assurer la compatibilité entre les systèmes.
 Configurer l’ordonnancement, la gestion des dépendances et les chargements incrémentiels de données afin de répondre aux exigences d’affaires.
 Respecter les normes de développement établies et enrichir la bibliothèque de composants d’intégration réutilisables.
 2. Fiabilité et soutien opérationnel 
 Surveiller les tâches d’intégration et analyser les anomalies, notamment les enregistrements manquants, les doublons et les écarts de données.
 Mettre en place des mécanismes de journalisation (logging), d’alertes, de tentatives automatiques (retries) et de reprise sur incident afin de simplifier l’exploitation et le soutien technique des intégrations.
 Valider l’exhaustivité et l’exactitude des données au moyen de rapprochements réguliers et de contrôles automatisés.
 Résoudre les problèmes touchant les systèmes sources, les processus d’intégration et les destinations finales, en étroite collaboration avec les équipes concernées.
 Optimiser la performance et la facilité de mise à jour des intégrations existantes.

 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes opérationnelles et techniques afin de clarifier les exigences de données, les cartographies, les dépendances et les critères d’acceptation.
 Travailler avec les ingénieurs de données et les spécialistes en ingénierie analytique pour fournir des flux d’entrée fiables en vue de la transformation et des rapports en aval, tout en participant aux initiatives communes reliant l’intégration et l’ingénierie analytique.
 Utiliser les outils de contrôle de version (Git), participer aux revues de code et soutenir les activités de test et de déploiement.
 Tenir à jour une documentation claire détaillant la logique d’intégration, les configurations, les dépendances et les procédures de soutien opérationnel.

 Expérience pratique de la programmation avec Python.
 Solide maîtrise du langage SQL pour l’extraction, la validation, le rapprochement et le dépannage des données.
 Expérience de travail avec les API REST, le format JSON ainsi que les formats de fichiers courants comme CSV et XML.
 Expérience liée à l’ordonnancement, à la gestion des erreurs, à la journalisation et à la résolution de pannes en environnement de production.
 Connaissance pratique de Git ainsi que des méthodes standard de développement, de test et de déploiement.
 Compétences et aptitudes: 
 Capacité à mener à bien un projet d’intégration bien défini, depuis la collecte des besoins jusqu’au développement, aux tests, au déploiement et au soutien technique.
 Rigueur méthodologique dans la résolution de problèmes et souci constant de l’exactitude des données.

 Providius is seeking an experienced, hands-on Accounting & Finance Lead to manage the company's accounting, payroll, and financial administration functions.
 This is an independent, individual-contributor role with broad responsibilities. You will oversee the day-to-day financial operations of the business, ensuring accurate records, timely payments, reliable payroll, and compliance with applicable requirements.
 Beyond routine accounting, you'll work directly with senior leadership to improve financial visibility through monthly reporting, budgeting, cash flow monitoring, and financial analysis. You'll also coordinate with our external accounting firm, which supports corporate taxation and year-end accounting.
 We're looking for someone with strong accounting fundamentals who enjoys taking ownership, solving problems, and working across different aspects of a business.
 This position offers an opportunity to move beyond a narrowly defined accounting role, gain exposure to business operations and financial decision-making, and help develop the financial processes and reporting capabilities of a growing technology company.
 Key Duties & Responsibilities
 1. Accounting Operations & Bookkeeping
 Independently manage day-to-day accounting operations, including the general ledger, journal entries, accruals, and reconciliations.
 Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records.
 Manage bank accounts, credit card transactions, expense reporting, and financial recordkeeping.
 Perform monthly account reconciliations and support the month-end closing process.
 Maintain organized records, accounting procedures, and appropriate internal controls.
 Identify and resolve accounting discrepancies, ensuring accuracy and completeness.
 2. Accounts Receivable & Accounts Payable
 Manage customer invoicing, accounts receivable, payment tracking, and collections.
 Process vendor invoices, accounts payable, payments, and employee expense reimbursements.
 Monitor outstanding receivables, payment schedules, and aging balances.
 Reconcile customer and vendor accounts.
 Handle foreign currency transactions involving international customers and suppliers.
 Coordinate with sales and operations teams on customer contracts, billing, and renewals.
 3. Payroll & Employee Administration
 Administer employee payroll through the company's payroll system, ensuring accurate and timely processing.
 Maintain employee compensation records, salary adjustments, vacation balances, and payroll-related information.
 Coordinate employee benefits enrolment, changes, and administration.
 Manage payroll reconciliations, statutory deductions, and year-end payroll reporting.
 Respond to routine employee payroll and benefits inquiries.
 Support general HR administration, employee documentation, and related administrative activities.
 4. Financial Reporting & Analysis
 Prepare monthly financial statements, including income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow reporting.
 Develop and maintain regular financial summaries and management reports for company leadership.
 Monitor financial performance, expenses, and cash flow.
 Prepare budget-to-actual comparisons and investigate significant variances.
 Assist with financial forecasting, budgeting, and expense planning.
 Identify opportunities to improve financial reporting, processes, and operational efficiency.
 Provide practical financial information and analysis to support management decisions.
 5. Taxation, Compliance & External Accounting
 Prepare and submit GST/HST returns and other routine financial remittances.
 Coordinate with the company's external accounting firm on year-end financial statements, corporate taxation, and related accounting matters.
 Prepare reconciliations, schedules, documentation, and supporting records for external accountants.
 Maintain compliance with applicable CRA requirements and accounting obligations.
 Support financial documentation and expense tracking for government funding programs, R&D activities, and tax incentives.
 6. Business & Financial Administration
 Support general business administration and operational activities as needed.
 Assist with tracking software licence revenue, maintenance contracts, recurring revenue, and deferred revenue.
 Help maintain financial records relating to projects, departments, and company initiatives.
 Improve existing accounting workflows, documentation, and administrative processes.
 Work directly with leadership to develop more effective financial reporting and planning practices as the company grows.
 About Providius
 Providius Corp. is a Canadian software technology company specializing in operational defence for mission-critical networks and infrastructure. Through AI-driven observability and network traffic analysis, Providius delivers software solutions that strengthen operational integrity, identify emerging risks, and improve the resilience of critical systems.
 Headquartered in Hamilton, Ontario, Providius serves enterprise customers across North America and internationally. As our company continues to grow and expand into new markets, we're looking for a capable accounting professional to take ownership of our day-to-day financial operations and help strengthen our financial reporting and planning capabilities
 Qualifications & Experience

 Degree or diploma in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
 At least 3 years of relevant accounting experience, with demonstrated responsibility for core accounting functions.
 Strong understanding of general ledger accounting, journal entries, reconciliations, and month-end processes.
 Experience preparing financial statements and financial reports.

 Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and commitment to accuracy.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based and is not an employment relationship.
 What this opportunity involves 
 We're looking for contributors to share their own medical lab report. You add the original files, and details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, and contact details, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. You also check the redacted preview before you submit. The lab's name and address, the test names, and the results stay in the report. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. The files help improve AI systems that read and understand medical documents. In this project, contributors may:
 Add the PDF file of their own lab report, for example blood test results;
 Take an iPhone photo of each printed page of the report and a screenshot of each page on an iPhone, iPad, or Mac;
 Check the redacted preview of each page and submit it only if all details that identify them are covered;
 Add one report per task;
 Submit clear files where every page of the report is fully visible.
 If you have your own lab test results and are comfortable sharing them once your personal details are covered, apply to take part in this project.
 What we look for

 To be 18 to 65 years old and live in one of these countries: the UK, Canada, Ireland, Germany, Switzerland, Poland, Portugal, Brazil, Spain, Türkiye, Norway, Indonesia, the UAE, or Israel (no VPN while using Mindrift);
 Their own medical lab report as a PDF file (1 to 10 pages): lab test results only, such as a blood count, blood chemistry, or a urine test;
 A report from a lab in the country where they live, preferably in the local language (reports in English, or in both languages, are also accepted);
 A printed copy of the report, an iPhone (any model) for the photos, and an iPhone, iPad, or Mac for the screenshots.

 Privacy
 Taking part is voluntary, and choosing not to take part doesn’t affect your Mindrift account. Before your first task, you read and sign a project consent form. Details that identify you, such as names, ID numbers, dates of birth, addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses, as well as doctors' names and signatures, are covered automatically and checked again during review before the report is used. Your original files are deleted. Once your report is accepted, it is no longer linked to you. We never ask you to send your report by email, chat or anywhere outside the Mindrift platform.
 Project time expectations

 The AI-Delivery Life Cycle Product Enablement Engineer combines product ownership with forward-deployed engineering to assure project delivery teams successfully adopt and use RBC's AI-Delivery Life Cycle Methodology & Platform. Working alongside project teams, this role removes adoption barriers, validates platform capabilities in real delivery scenarios, and aligns the platform to evolving project needs. Every decision - from backlog prioritization to field support - is driven by the value it delivers to users.

 Product owner as the voice of the user: Representing the needs, priorities, and friction of delivery teams to the AI-DLC Platform engineering team - ensuring what gets built next is shaped by what users actually need and ordered by the value it delivers. Translating field insight into well-formed requirements with clear acceptance criteria, dependencies, and traceability, and maintaining a value-driven backlog in partnership with engineering. 
 Release readiness: Maintaining a groomed, estimation-ready backlog aligned to the release plan, identifying scope risks and dependency conflicts early, and keeping delivery and adoption status visible to product leadership and stakeholders. 
 User enablement: Working alongside project and large program teams adopting AI-DLC to understand their delivery context and provide proactive hands-on support with agentic workflows and tools so they can use the platform effectively.

A key outcome of each bootcamp is a seeded project context from which business and technical members of the team can start using the AI-DLC platform on their project immediately. 
 Field gap resolution: Facilitating working sessions that identify where platform capabilities or workflows fall short. Investigating product friction, distinguishing platform gaps from enablement needs, and coordinating the right response - whether a code fix, a new skill, or better documentation - and feeding patterns back into the product roadmap to prevent recurrence. 
 User guides and communications: Producing clear, well-structured user guides, guided experiences, newsletters, blog posts, videos, and other communications so teams can self-serve and adopt the platform without waiting for hands-on support. 
 Leadership & community partnerships: Taking ownership of the platform's adoption narrative across RBC - incubating and leading a Community Contribution model where innovators contribute capabilities, build agentic workflows, and share reusable practices atop the AI-DLC platform.

 Experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, Delivery Lead, Forward Deployed Engineer, or in a comparable product-delivery role.

 Strong technical writing skills -- able to produce clear user guides and enablement content for both technical and non-technical audiences. 
 Demonstrated ability to facilitate working sessions, engage delivery team stakeholders, and drive alignment on ambiguous, cross-functional problems. 
 A practical, field-oriented approach with the ability to move between roadmap discussions, backlog decisions, content creation, and hands-on enablement.

 A full-stack or front-end development background with the ability to build interactive experiences both digital and agentic. 
 Experience designing and facilitating bootcamps, workshops, or applied learning programs.

 As a Product Marketing Manager, Defense & Security, you will play a strategic role in accelerating the growth of CAE's global Defense & Security business. You will develop market-leading positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategies for a portfolio of training, simulation, mission support, and digital solutions that enhance military readiness, operational effectiveness, and force modernization across air, land, maritime, cyber, space, and multi-domain operations.

You will help shape strategic pursuits, influence customer perceptions, and strengthen CAE's position as a trusted partner in defense readiness and training transformation.
 Positioning
 Acquire subject matter expertise on the global defense and security landscape, including military training modernization, force readiness requirements, operational concepts, defense acquisition processes, and emerging defense technologies.
 Develop differentiated positioning, messaging, and thought leadership that resonate with military operators, training and education commands, procurement authorities, defense ministries, government agencies, and defense prime contractors.

 Collaborate with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, and Business Development teams to launch and position new defense training, simulation, synthetic environment, mission support, and digital transformation capabilities.

 Develop content and messaging that supports strategic growth priorities across domestic, allied, and international defense markets.
 Market Insights

 Analyze geopolitical, operational, and technological trends that influence military preparedness, defense investment decisions, and customer requirements.
